chapter: National Guard band and first jobs in Chicago
title: The 8th Illinois National Guard band at about sixteen
summary: He joined the 370th Eighth Illinois Infantry National Guard band, stationed in Chicago, and got good reading and concert training.

blocks.x: When were you -- now, when you went in this Army band, what was that? I mean --
That was the 370th Eighth Illinois (unintelligible) infantry National Guard band. And some of us fellows. And Dornell Howard was in that band too.
Well, you didn't -- I mean this wasn't like the real Army. This was the National Guard.
I see. So you didn't leave Chicago with (unintelligible).
Because when I was reading that, I thought, well, you'd be much too young.

That's right. Yeah. was we all started to -- say, let's go enlist into the National Guard and get some good, you know, -- learning they were the playing that the Chicago ones played all type of music. So Hamp -- they had a-(unintelligible) with the colored publication, paper there. Hamp, Defender he went in to the Chicago Defender band, and we went into the Eighth Illinois North Infantry Band.
Yeah, but you got good tuition, though.
Oh, very good tuition played all the (unintelligible) big symphonics, big overtures, and then you played them big band marches, and then you played the concerts too.

Yeah, well this is where, I take it, that in some respects a city like Chicago or New York, you'd be a bit ahead of musicians coming from other parts of the country because they -- many of those early players couldn't read at all.
Yeah. And then when all those theaters are going in Chicago, and you got to read for them.
